stem: Before drawing any conclusion, the team will ___ the survey responses for recurring patterns.
explanationPerOption: Correct. The slot needs a transitive verb meaning to examine in detail; 'analyze' takes 'responses' as its object.
A noun meaning a comparison. It cannot follow 'will' as a main verb, and it does not mean to examine.
A noun naming a loss of movement. Orthographically close to the answer but semantically unrelated.
A verb, but it means to declare publicly, which contradicts 'before drawing any conclusion'.

stem: The committee could not ___ the two accounts of the incident, since each contradicted the other on every material point.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Reconcile' means to make two conflicting accounts consistent, which is exactly what contradiction prevents.
To identify something already known. The problem is not identification but conflict.
To advise in favour of. One does not recommend two accounts to each other.
To think again about. Possible grammatically, but it leaves the contradiction unexplained.

stem: Researchers must ___ the reliability of a source before citing it as evidence.
explanationPerOption: To help. A phonetic neighbour of the answer, but one does not help a source's reliability.
Correct. 'Assess' means to evaluate or judge, which is what one does to reliability.
A noun meaning a useful resource. Wrong part of speech for the slot after 'must'.
To state confidently. One asserts a claim, not the reliability of a source one has yet to judge.

stem: The author's argument is ___ rather than stated outright, and readers who skim the introduction will miss it entirely.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Implicit' means suggested without being directly expressed, which the contrast with 'stated outright' requires.
Means unappeasable. Shares a prefix with the answer but does not concern how something is expressed.
Means unbelievable. The sentence is about how the argument is conveyed, not whether it is credible.
Means essential or commanding. Would not contrast with 'stated outright'.

stem: Because the wording of the clause was ___, two courts reached opposite readings of the same contract.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation, which is precisely what two opposite readings demonstrate.
Means strongly desirous of success. A phonetic neighbour, but wording cannot be ambitious in this sense.
Means willing to comply. Does not explain why readings diverged.
Means made louder or larger. Amplified wording would be clearer, not more disputable.

stem: The distinction the paper draws is ___: it rests on no principle the author is willing to state, and shifts from case to case.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Arbitrary' means based on personal whim rather than reason or system, which the absence of a stated principle establishes.
Means settled by an arbitrator. A shared root, but the sentence describes no dispute resolution.
Means clearly expressed. The colon explains the opposite: the author will not state the principle.
Means man-made or contrived. Close in spirit but does not capture the absence of any governing rule.

stem: A grant of this size should ___ the fieldwork the project has postponed for two seasons.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Facilitate' means to make an action easier, which funding does for postponed fieldwork.
Means to congratulate. A close phonetic neighbour with an entirely unrelated meaning.
Means to invent or construct falsely. A grant does not fabricate fieldwork.
Means to vary irregularly. Intransitive here, so it cannot take 'the fieldwork' as an object.

stem: The findings are ___ with the earlier study, though the two used samples drawn from populations that barely overlap.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Coherent with' means logically consistent with, which is what a comparison of findings asserts.
Means sticking together as a unit. Describes internal unity, not agreement between two separate studies.
Means occupying the same place or time. The sentence compares content, not position.
Means happening at the same time. 'Though' signals a concession about method, not timing.

stem: The editor asked the author to ___ the term in the opening paragraph, since readers outside the field would not know it.
explanationPerOption: To improve by small changes. One cannot refine a term readers have never met.
To restrict within limits. A phonetic neighbour, but confining a term does not help an unfamiliar reader.
Correct. 'Define' means to state the precise meaning, which is what an unfamiliar reader needs.
To refuse, or to decrease. Neither sense fits an instruction about an unfamiliar term.

stem: The model ___ its predictions from three variables, none of which is measured directly.
explanationPerOption: Means to take something away from someone. It takes a person as object, not predictions.
Correct. 'Derive X from Y' means to obtain X from a source, which matches the 'from three variables' structure.
Intransitive in this sense and does not take 'from' with an object of origin in the required way.
Means to throw into disorder. Unrelated to producing predictions.

stem: Please do not ___ the speaker; questions will be taken at the end.
explanationPerOption: Means to explain the meaning of something. One interprets a text, not a speaker mid-sentence.
Means to insert a remark. Closer, but it is typically used of the remark, not with the speaker as object.
Correct. 'Interrupt' takes a person as object and means to break in on them while they are speaking.
Means to cross. Geometric, not conversational.

stem: The reform will ___ several agencies whose functions currently overlap.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Consolidate' means to combine into a single more effective whole, which is the remedy for overlapping functions.
Means to comfort someone in distress. Takes a person as object.
Means to form or make up. A reform that constituted agencies would create them, not merge existing ones.
Means to interpret. One construes a text or a rule, not an agency.

stem: A single sentence can change meaning entirely when the surrounding ___ is removed.
explanationPerOption: Means a competition. Nothing in the sentence concerns rivalry.
Means the material contained in something. Close, but content is what the sentence contains, not what surrounds it.
Correct. 'Context' is the surrounding text or circumstances that fix a sentence's meaning.
Means touch or communication. Not something that surrounds a sentence.

stem: The data ___ a trend, but the sample is too small for the pattern to be called established.
explanationPerOption: Means to devote to a purpose. Data cannot dedicate a trend.
Correct. 'Indicate' means to point to or suggest, which is the appropriately tentative verb before 'but the sample is too small'.
Means to clear of blame or to justify. Too strong given the concession that follows.
Means to renounce a throne or duty. Unrelated.

stem: The argument ___ of three claims, the last of which does not follow from the first two.
explanationPerOption: Means to continue stubbornly. It does not take 'of' with a list of parts.
Correct. 'Consist of' means to be composed of, which introduces the three claims.
Means to withstand. Takes a direct object, not 'of'.
Means to demand firmly. Takes 'on' or a clause, not a list of components.

stem: The paper is careful to ___ correlation from causation, a distinction its critics accuse it of blurring elsewhere.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Distinguish X from Y' means to recognise the difference between them, which 'a distinction' confirms.
Means to put out a fire. A phonetic neighbour with no relevant sense.
Means to make smaller. Does not take the 'X from Y' structure in this sense.
Means to share out. One distributes goods, not one concept from another.

stem: The study was designed to ___ which of the two treatments produced the faster recovery.
explanationPerOption: A noun meaning who or what someone is. Wrong part of speech after 'to'.
Means to compensate for loss. Legal or financial, not investigative.
Correct. 'Identify' means to establish which thing something is, matching 'which of the two'.
Means to make more intense. The study establishes a fact rather than strengthening anything.

stem: Any serious account of the period must ___ the economic pressures that preceded the reforms.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Involve' means to include as a necessary part, which is what a serious account must do with those pressures.
Means to develop gradually. Intransitive here; an account does not evolve pressures.
Means to turn about an axis, or with 'around', to have as a main concern. Requires 'around' to take this object.
Means to transfer power downward. Unrelated to what an account must contain.

stem: Although the ___ for inclusion were published in advance, reviewers applied them so unevenly that the shortlist tells us little.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Criteria' is the plural form and agrees with the plural verb 'were published'.
The singular form. It would require 'was published', so the verb rules it out.
Means critical assessments. Reviewers apply standards, not assessments, for inclusion.
The plural of crisis. Nothing in the sentence concerns emergencies.

stem: From the fragmentary records the historian was able to ___ a chronology that no single document supplies.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Deduce' means to reach a conclusion by reasoning from available evidence, which fragmentary records require.
Means to lead astray. A phonetic neighbour with no scholarly sense.
Means to make smaller. The historian builds a chronology rather than shrinking one.
Means to formally admit someone to a post. Takes a person as object.

stem: The report will ___ its central claim with three case studies drawn from different regions.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Illustrate' means to make clear by example, which is exactly the function of case studies.
Means to light up, or figuratively to clarify. Possible in loose usage, but it does not take examples as its instrument in this construction.
An adjective meaning not authorised. Wrong part of speech after 'will'.
Means to remove entirely. The report supports its claim rather than removing it.

stem: The author never says the policy failed; the judgement is left to ___ from the figures in the appendix.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Emerge' means to become apparent gradually, which is how an unstated judgement arises from data.
Means to submerge in liquid, or to absorb oneself. Takes an object or a reflexive.
Means to leave one's country. A phonetic neighbour with no relevant sense.
Means to combine into one. Figures do not merge a judgement.

stem: The new regulations ___ how much of the catch a single vessel may land in one season.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Restrict' means to set a limit on quantity or extent, which a catch limit does.
Means to hold back physically or emotionally. Usually takes a person or an impulse as object.
Means to withstand. Regulations do not resist a quantity.
Means to alter after review. The sentence states a limit, not a change to one.

stem: What the essay presents as a ___ reading of the treaty is in fact one interpretation among several, and not the most widely held.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Definitive' means authoritative and final, which is precisely the claim the second clause overturns.
Means protective against attack. Does not set up the contrast with 'one interpretation among several'.
Means showing respect. A deferential reading would not conflict with being one among several.
Means capable of being defined. Too weak to be contradicted by the rest of the sentence.

stem: The two departments were asked to ___ their schedules so that the shared equipment would not sit idle.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Coordinate' takes schedules as a direct object and means to bring them into an efficient relationship.
Means to confirm with supporting evidence. One corroborates a claim, not a schedule.
Means to match, or to exchange letters. In the matching sense it takes 'to' or 'with', not a direct object.
Means to work together. Intransitive, so it cannot take 'their schedules' directly.

stem: The committee's remit is deliberately narrow: it may ___ evidence but may not act on it.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Obtain' means to acquire or get, which pairs with the restriction that follows.
Means to achieve or reach a goal. One attains a standard, not evidence.
Means to refrain, and takes 'from'. It cannot take 'evidence' as a direct object.
Means to order officially or to confer holy orders. Unrelated.

stem: Each chapter ends with a summary that ___ the main points for the reader.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Recap' means to state the main points again briefly, which is the function of a summary.
Means to fall back into a former state, typically illness. Intransitive.
Means to present in a different form. A summary restates rather than reshapes.
Means to withdraw a statement. A summary confirms rather than withdraws.

stem: The trial was halted not because the drug proved harmful but because its benefit over the placebo was too ___ to justify continuing.
explanationPerOption: Correct. 'Slight' means small in degree, which explains halting a trial whose benefit was negligible.
The past participle of a verb meaning to insult. Wrong part of speech for the slot after 'too'.
A noun meaning dexterity, as in 'sleight of hand'. A homophone with no adjectival use.
Means very great. It would reverse the logic: a severe benefit would argue for continuing.

stem: Funding was withdrawn ___ the project had met every milestone in its original proposal.
explanationPerOption: Correct. Meeting every milestone would normally protect funding, so the clause is concessive and requires a contrast connector.
Reverses the logic: meeting milestones is not a reason to withdraw funding.
Expresses purpose. Withdrawal was not undertaken in order to meet milestones.
Expresses time. It would imply the milestones triggered the withdrawal, which is the same inversion as 'because'.

stem: The instrument is accurate to within a millimetre; ___, it is useless in the field, where vibration exceeds that margin many times over.
explanationPerOption: Correct. High accuracy would normally suggest usefulness, so the reversal requires a concessive connector.
Signals a result. Accuracy does not cause uselessness; the field conditions do.
Signals likeness. The two clauses stand in opposition, not parallel.
Signals addition. It would make uselessness a further virtue alongside accuracy.
